Propose Columns to Draw by Approximate Bayesian Bootstrap

Source: R/mi_pca_abb.R
abb_cols.Rd

Find the columns of a matrix of proportions, such as DNAm beta values, whose observed values lie almost all near 0 or almost all near 1. Pass the result as abb to mipca(), mipca_tune() or mipca_flank_plan().

Usage

abb_cols(obj, bound = 0.02, q = 0.95)

Arguments

obj

A double matrix with samples in rows and features in columns. Row and column names are required and must be unique. Every observed value must lie in [0, 1].

bound

Numeric. A value below bound counts as near 0, and a value above 1 - bound as near 1. Must be above 0 and below 0.5. Defaults to 0.02.

q

Numeric. Proportion of a column's observed values that must be near 0, or near 1, for the column to be listed. Must be above 0.5 and at most 1. Defaults to 0.95.

Value

An integer vector of column numbers in obj, in increasing order. It is empty when no column is listed, and abb takes it as no list.

Details

The listed columns. A column listed in abb is left out of the model, and its missing values are drawn from its own observed values by approximate Bayesian bootstrap (Rubin and Schenker 1986). Unlike the model, this keeps the exact 0s and 1s such columns often hold. Each column is drawn on its own, so its relation to the other columns is not kept. mipca_tune() tunes on the other columns, and summary() does not report the listed ones.

Choosing the list. The defaults list only the most extreme columns. Raise bound or lower q to list more, or pass any columns to abb. A column with no observed values is never listed.

References

Rubin DB, Schenker N (1986). Multiple imputation for interval estimation from simple random samples with ignorable nonresponse. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 81(394), 366-374. doi:10.1080/01621459.1986.10478280

See also

  • mipca() to fit with the list.

  • mipca_flank_plan(), which leaves the listed columns out of every window.

Examples

set.seed(1)
sim <- sim_mat(n = 50, p = 20, beta = TRUE)
obj <- sim$input

# Push two columns against 0 and 1
obj[, 3] <- obj[, 3] / 100
obj[, 4] <- 1 - (1 - obj[, 4]) / 100

abb <- abb_cols(obj)
abb
#> [1] 3 4

fit <- mipca(obj, rank = 2, transform = "logit_biwhiten", seed = 1, abb = abb)
fit
#> si_mi fit: 50 x 20, 100 imputed cells, 400 draws
#>   next: as.matrix() with 'draw' for a completed matrix, summary() for Rhat and ESS
